Paul is saying that he wasn’t there yet, but he was single minded in pressing forward to obtain the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. Paul was the most successful minister of the Gospel that ever lived, and wrote more of the New Testament of the Bible than anyone else, and had a greater revelation of the Grace of God and the true Gospel than anyone else. He did all this by being single minded, and forgetting the things in his past, and kept pressing forward toward his goal. Keeping our minds upon Jesus will enable us to be effective ministers of the Gospel, if that is where we keep our focus. Staying focused on God, at all times should be the goal of all Christians.

Paul didn’t want to just be a successful minister, but he was pressing on toward the highest of honors with God. We could learn a lot by studying Paul’s life and service, and if we would be as dedicated to the Gospel as he was, we also could make a real difference in this world we live in. Most of us Christians get too wrapped up in the daily happenings in this world (Matthew 13:22), and let it keep our minds from being focused on God. Keep God’s Word in your mind and heart all day, every day, and try to make a difference in this world like the Apostle Paul did. Do you think you are just to busy to stay focused on God’s Word all day? You need to realize that the same part of you that can worry all day about something wrong in your life is the same part of you that can think on the Word all day.
